assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of proglucagon-derived GLP-1 as an incretin and its development into long-acting agonists has transformed diabetes care and obesity treatment, with cardiovascular and renal outcome benefits. The discovery chain from physiology to drug is clear and the impact is very large and still expanding.
assessment.attribution: Drucker (GLP-1 biology, intestinotrophic GLP-2), Holst (incretin physiology and secretion) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1 peptide) are the core scientific contributors; Knudsen is credited for the pharmaceutical engineering of liraglutide/semaglutide and is the likely competing fourth name. Habener and Mojsov priority questions, and the three-person limit, make allocation delicate.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent, large randomized outcome trials and broad clinical adoption; mechanism and effect are stable. Recognition appears timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among basic discoverers versus drug developers is contested and the three-person limit excludes Knudsen.
Long-term safety and the central mechanisms of weight loss are still being characterized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Light-gated channels (channelrhodopsins) allowing millisecond control of defined cell types created a method that reshaped neuroscience and cardiac and retinal physiology. The originality and breadth of impact are exceptional, and the method is used in thousands of laboratories.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) identified and characterized channelrhodopsin; Deisseroth (and Boyden) showed its use in neurons and in vivo with cell-type targeting. Miesenboeck's earlier genetically targeted photoactivation adds a priority complication; at most three names can be chosen from six credited.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and mature; therapeutic translation (retinal optogenetics) is emerging. Recognition is timely given two decades of validated use.
uncertainties: Six credible contributors for a three-person limit; Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck are disadvantaged.
Clinical impact is early compared with research impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational inhibition of the BCR-ABL kinase with imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal into a manageable disease and established the proof of principle for targeted kinase-inhibitor therapy. It is a clean, well-understood link from molecular lesion to cure-like clinical outcome.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development at Ciba-Geigy/Novartis), Druker (clinical translation and proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a defensible trio. Rowley's and Witte's earlier discovery work on the oncogene lies outside the supplied credit and may be seen as a gap.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of long-term survival data and strong independent confirmation; the interpretation is stable and recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: The prize might be considered to depend on earlier BCR-ABL discovery work not credited here.
Imatinib's discovery involved a team beyond the three named.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed against CD19 produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and have opened a new class of living therapeutics. The concept, engineering design and clinical results are strong.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical CD19 CAR-T and costimulation), Sadelain (CD28 costimulated CARs and design principles) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T-cell trials) are plausible. Eshhar, Kuwana and Brenner/Gross priority could complicate fair attribution, and the first-generation CAR concept is not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and strong independent confirmation in hematologic cancers; solid tumours, toxicity and cost remain open.
uncertainties: Foundational chimeric receptor credit (e.g. Eshhar) is not among the credited names.
Benefit in solid tumours is unproven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and elucidation of mTORC1/mTORC2 as central integrators of nutrient and growth signals created a framework spanning growth control, metabolism, aging, immunosuppression and cancer. The discovery is fundamental and highly original.
assessment.attribution: Hall (genetic discovery of TOR) is the clear primary figure; Schreiber (FKBP12-rapamycin as a ligand) and Sabatini (mammalian mTOR pathway components) are strong secondary contributors. Brown/Sabatini and Heitman/Hall priority claims on mammalian TOR need weighing.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature with extensive independent confirmation; clinical use of rapalogs is established, though broad therapeutic payoffs are mixed.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and other contributors is unresolved.
Therapeutic translation has been less dramatic than the basic science.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of the unfolded protein response as an ER-to-nucleus signalling pathway (Ire1, Hac1/Xbp1 splicing) revealed a core principle of quality control and stress signalling relevant to secretory, metabolic and neurodegenerative disease. It is conceptually clean and original.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the central pair with complementary discoveries (Ire1 and Hac1 splicing; ATF6 and mammalian UPR). Others such as Ron or Kaufman could be argued for the mammalian branches, but a Walter-Mori pairing is reasonably clean.
assessment.maturity: Mature with Lasker recognition and extensive confirmation across organisms; disease relevance is more incremental and therapeutic translation is early.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact has not yet matured.
Mammalian UPR branches involve additional investigators outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus or thalamus transformed the treatment of advanced Parkinson's disease and tremor, and gave a causal circuit-level handle on motor control. The clinical benefit is large and durable, and the field has expanded to other disorders.
assessment.attribution: Benabid is the single credited name and the decisive figure for high-frequency stimulation. Others such as Delong (subthalamic circuit model) are not in the supplied credit, which could make a single-laureate award less balanced.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of clinical use and randomized trial evidence; recognition is mature and not premature, though mechanism of action remains debated.
uncertainties: Mechanism of therapeutic action is incompletely understood.
Credit for the underlying basal ganglia circuit model sits outside the credited names.
Clinical-device work may fit the prize criteria less cleanly than a biological discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING as the pathway sensing cytosolic DNA and driving type I interferon responses defined a new innate immune axis relevant to infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and senescence. It is original and clearly changed the field.
assessment.attribution: Chen (identification of cGAS and cGAMP as second messenger) is the decisive contributor; Barber (STING) is the other core figure. Other names (Ishikawa, Wu, Sun) are co-authors rather than likely recipients; Vance, Patel and others are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly validated across many groups, but therapeutic translation is early and the pathway's disease roles are still being refined, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Clinical impact is not yet demonstrated.
Credit among STING discoverers (Barber, Ishikawa, Ishikawa/Barber, Tao, Sun) has been debated.
